slides.title: Pilot design and power: size from evidence
slides.claim: A convenient sample is not proof of an economically meaningful effect.
body: For two independent arms, n ≈ 2(zα/2 + zβ)²σ²/δ² per arm. Cluster design effect = 1 + (m − 1)ICC.
Chosen σ=10, δ=5, α=.05 and 80% power imply about 63 observations per arm before clustering or attrition.
With 10 customers per cluster and ICC=.10, the design effect is 1.9: about 120 adjusted observations per arm.
Actual route variance, balance, spillovers and attrition determine the final sample. No actual sample size is approved.

calculations.question: Reported margin
calculations.limit: Using rounded revenue of USD28.7bn gives 2.4519%; keep the same entity, period and currency.
calculations.sensitivity: Revenue can grow while margin falls.

calculations.question: Demand to delivered sales
calculations.formula: Population × demand per person × access × capture, capped by delivery
calculations.limit: Demand, access and capture are chosen inputs. Unmet orders cannot count as revenue.
calculations.sensitivity: If route capacity reaches 9,000t, plant capacity still caps delivery at 8,000t.

calculations.question: Volume, revenue and EBITDA
calculations.formula: Volume × net price; volume × unit cost; contribution less fixed cash cost
calculations.substitution: 100,000t × USD400/t = USD40m revenue; costs = USD34m; contribution = USD6m; less USD2m fixed cost = USD4m EBITDA.
calculations.limit: EBITDA omits cash tax, capital spending and working cash. These are chosen saleable-volume and net-price inputs.
calculations.sensitivity: A USD10/t price change at unchanged volume changes EBITDA by USD1m.

calculations.question: Yield and by-products
calculations.formula: Input = main output / yield; output, by-product and loss sum to input
calculations.limit: By-products may earn revenue. Their quality, price and conversion cost need evidence.
calculations.sensitivity: At 95% main yield, input is 105,263t. Reconcile the remaining mass separately.

calculations.question: Customer cost per usable output
calculations.formula: Purchase and preparation cost / usable output
calculations.substitution: Offer A: (USD30 + USD5) / 45kg = USD0.7778/kg. Offer B: (USD32 + USD4) / 48kg = USD0.7500/kg.
calculations.result: B costs 3.57% less per usable kg
calculations.limit: Chosen flour-like inputs. Paid adoption also depends on cash, trust and availability.
calculations.sensitivity: If B produces only 45kg, cost rises to USD0.80/kg and reverses the advantage.

calculations.question: Pack cash and cost per meal
calculations.formula: Cash ticket differs from cost per use; assume 100g dry input per meal
calculations.substitution: Small: (₦600 + ₦100 prep) / 5 meals = ₦140/meal. Large: (₦2,000 + ₦400 prep) / 20 meals = ₦120/meal.
calculations.result: Small cash ticket ₦600; large pack 14.29% cheaper per meal
calculations.limit: Chosen Nigerian cash units and serving size. The large pack needs more upfront cash.
calculations.sensitivity: Large purchase cash is 3.33 times the small pack, despite lower cost per meal.

calculations.question: Percent versus percentage points
calculations.formula: Distinguish absolute percentage-point change from relative percentage change
calculations.limit: A margin change is not the same measure as revenue growth.
calculations.sensitivity: On USD100 revenue, profit rises from USD8 to USD10.

calculations.question: Profit to free cash
calculations.formula: EBIT less tax, plus D&A, less maintenance/growth capex and change in NWC
calculations.limit: Assume no prior tax losses, 25% tax, USD0.6m maintenance and USD0.4m growth capex.
calculations.sensitivity: If NWC does not increase, this period’s cash rises by USD1m.

calculations.question: Working-capital release
calculations.formula: Revenue basis for receivables; cost basis for inventory; DPO unchanged
calculations.substitution: AR: USD40m × 5 / 365 = USD0.547945m. Inventory: USD34m × 7 / 365 = USD0.652055m. Total = USD1.20m.
calculations.limit: All sales are credit in this example. The transition release is not recurring annual profit.
calculations.sensitivity: One further DSO day releases USD0.109589m at this sales base.

calculations.question: Inherited Nigeria screen
calculations.formula: Inherited additive uplift and sales-day proxy; ramped three-year DCF
calculations.limit: NGN4.2bn initial capital; 28% hurdle; 50/80/100% benefit ramp. Tax, replacement and actual cash bases are absent.
calculations.sensitivity: Repair procurement FX overlap, AR/inventory/AP, capex, tax and currency before a production decision.

calculations.question: FX and commodity interaction
calculations.formula: Local imported cost = USD commodity price × local currency per USD
calculations.limit: Both shocks hit the same procurement base. Hedge effects need documented contracts.
calculations.sensitivity: Chosen 70% cost pass-through recovers 14.7% initially; weaker customer volume may reduce retained margin.

calculations.question: Finite NPV and commissioning
calculations.formula: Discount each dated free cash flow; do not compare only undiscounted totals
calculations.limit: No terminal value. Staging USD3m now and USD2m in year 1, with cash in years 2–4, gives −USD0.2966m.
calculations.sensitivity: Paying USD5m now with a one-year cash delay gives −USD0.4784m.

calculations.question: Real and nominal consistency
calculations.formula: Consistent inflation of both cash and discount rate preserves NPV
calculations.result: Real and nominal three-year NPVs both −USD0.0263m
calculations.limit: Nominal cash grows by 5% inflation and is discounted at 15.5%. Project and currency risk require separate care.
calculations.sensitivity: Mixing nominal cash with a real hurdle overstates value.

calculations.question: Operating versus investment break-even
calculations.formula: Operating break-even pays fixed cash cost; investment break-even also pays capital
calculations.substitution: USD2m / (USD400 − USD340 per tonne) = 33,333t; / 150,000t capacity = 22.22% utilization.
calculations.result: Operating 33,333t; investment boundary 104,862 initial order tonnes
calculations.limit: Full NPV includes ramp, tax, replacement, working cash and the finite horizon.
calculations.sensitivity: Operating above 22.22% utilization can still give negative investment NPV.

calculations.question: Scenario weights are not likelihood
calculations.formula: Weighted average = sum of chosen weight × conditional NPV
calculations.limit: The central USD10m case is not a calibrated most-likely future. The adverse loss can breach funding.
calculations.sensitivity: If adverse weight is 0.5 and central weight 0.3, the mean becomes −USD0.6m.

calculations.question: Loss-tail VaR and CVaR
calculations.formula: Loss = max(0, −NPV); a quantile differs from the mean of a chosen tail
calculations.substitution: NPVs [−8, −4, 0, 2, 6] imply losses [0, 0, 0, 4, 8]. Nearest-rank VaR80 = 4; worst-20% CVaR80 = 8 (USDm).
calculations.result: Loss VaR80 USD4m; tail CVaR80 USD8m
calculations.limit: Declare discrete tie treatment: mean(loss ≥ VaR) would be USD6m here, a different convention.
calculations.sensitivity: Stress code uses mean(loss ≥ 95% quantile). Its chosen continuous generator has negligible ties.

calculations.question: Common-exposure diversification
calculations.formula: Equal individual average losses can conceal different joint tail exposures
calculations.substitution: Each source loses USD10m with chosen probability 0.2. A shared port produces joint loss USD20m with probability 0.2; independent joint probability is 0.04.
calculations.result: Expected total loss USD4m in both; joint tail differs
calculations.limit: Chosen probabilities illustrate dependence. Country flags do not remove a shared crop season or port.
calculations.sensitivity: A different basin without a different port can leave route exposure unchanged.

calculations.question: Difference in differences
calculations.formula: Subtract the counterfactual change from the treated change
calculations.limit: Parallel trends and no material spillovers are required. Four chosen means cannot support an estimated interval.
calculations.sensitivity: At USD2 contribution/unit, gross incremental contribution is USD40 before service and pilot cost.

calculations.question: Incremental ROMI
calculations.formula: Net incremental contribution after marketing / marketing spend
calculations.substitution: Incremental contribution 120 − service 20 − trade 10 − cannibalisation 10 = 80. Marketing spend 40. Net ROMI = (80 − 40)/40 = 100%.
calculations.limit: All inputs are chosen currency-thousands. Use a paid-sales counterfactual and full incremental costs.
calculations.sensitivity: If contribution after other costs is only 40, net ROMI is zero. Multi-year proposals need NPV.

calculations.question: Decision value of information
calculations.formula: Optimal decision value after information less before information, study and delay costs
calculations.substitution: Good state p=0.5: investment NPV 10; bad state p=0.5: −8; wait 0. Best prior EV=1; perfect-information EV=5; less study 1 and delay 0.5 gives net gain 2.5.
calculations.limit: A perfect study is an upper bound. Do not add its benefit again to a policy that already includes learning.
calculations.sensitivity: An imperfect pilot may be worth less than its cost; keep the wait option.

calculations.question: Reverse stress
calculations.formula: Solve the full NPV root and monitor the mechanism that moves it
calculations.substitution: The managed owned template reaches zero NPV at 104,862 initial annual order tonnes. The current 100,000t base needs 4.86% more initial orders.
calculations.limit: The threshold depends on cost, hurdle, tax and capacity; volume cannot repair a negative unit contribution.
calculations.sensitivity: Cost, FX or commissioning shocks shift the boundary. Monitor orders together with cash.

calculations.question: Size ranking can reverse
calculations.formula: Delivered units × unit contribution less fixed cost, then full cash-flow valuation
calculations.substitution: Country A: demand 200kt, capture 50kt, unit contribution USD20, fixed USD0.7m → EBITDA USD0.3m. B: demand 100kt, capture 40kt, contribution USD40 → USD0.9m.
calculations.result: B has 3 times EBITDA despite half the category size
calculations.limit: A and B are fictional teaching cases. Chosen capex USD5m vs USD2m and NWC USD2m vs USD0.5m further favour testing B.
calculations.sensitivity: Before capital differences, A overtakes B above 80kt captured at USD20/t while B stays at 40kt.
